explanation: Muscat is the port capital and administrative centre of Oman, located along the Gulf of Oman.

text: What is the highest mountain peak on the African continent?
explanation: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the highest peak in Africa, standing at 5,895 metres.

text: In which city do the White Nile and the Blue Nile meet to form the main Nile River?
explanation: The White Nile and Blue Nile converge at Khartoum, the capital of Sudan, to form the primary stem of the river.

text: Which river flows directly through the Iraqi capital, Baghdad?
explanation: The Tigris originates in the Taurus Mountains of Turkey and flows through Baghdad before joining the Euphrates.

text: What is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea by surface area?
explanation: Sicily covers approximately 25,711 square kilometres, making it the Mediterranean's largest island, ahead of Sardinia.

text: What is the capital city of Brazil, which was planned and inaugurated in 1960?
explanation: Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro to encourage economic development in the interior of the country.

text: Which saline lake between Jordan and the West Bank constitutes the lowest land elevation on Earth?
explanation: The shores of the Dead Sea lie more than 430 metres below sea level, making it Earth's lowest dry land.

text: What is the longest continental mountain range in the world, located in South America?
explanation: The Andes stretch for over 7,000 kilometres along the western coast of South America through seven countries.

text: Which strategic strait connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman?
explanation: About a fifth of the world's petroleum passes through the narrow waters of the Strait of Hormuz.

text: What has been the federal capital city of Nigeria since 1991?
explanation: Nigeria moved its official capital from coastal Lagos to the centrally planned city of Abuja in 1991.

text: Which mountain range is traditionally considered the natural boundary between Europe and Asia?
explanation: The Ural Mountains run north-to-south through western Russia and form the conventional border between Europe and Asia.

text: In which ocean are the Maldives located?
explanation: The Maldives archipelago is situated in the Indian Ocean, southwest of Sri Lanka and India.

text: Which African country is completely enclaved within the borders of South Africa?
explanation: The Kingdom of Lesotho is entirely encircled by South Africa, making it an enclaved sovereign nation.

text: What is the capital city of New Zealand?
explanation: Wellington, situated at the southern tip of the North Island, has been New Zealand's capital since 1865.

text: Which major river in West Africa forms a crescent loop through Mali, Niger, and Nigeria?
explanation: The Niger River is Africa's third-longest river, following the Nile and the Congo.

text: Which South American desert is regarded as the driest non-polar desert on Earth?
explanation: The Atacama Desert in northern Chile experiences hyperarid conditions, with some areas receiving virtually no rain.

text: What is the capital city of Mauritania?
explanation: Nouakchott was selected to be the national capital shortly before Mauritania's independence in 1960.

text: Which mountain range separates the Iberian Peninsula from the rest of continental Europe?
explanation: The Pyrenees form a natural barrier along the border of France and Spain, enclosing the microstate of Andorra.

text: Which strait connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean?
explanation: The Bab-el-Mandeb Strait lies between Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula and Djibouti and Eritrea in Africa.

text: What is the largest peninsula in the world by area?
explanation: The Arabian Peninsula covers over 3.2 million square kilometres across southwestern Asia.

text: What is the capital and largest city of Kenya?
explanation: Nairobi was founded in 1899 as a rail depot and grew rapidly to become the capital of Kenya.

text: Which sea separates the eastern coast of the Italian Peninsula from the Balkans?
explanation: The Adriatic Sea separates Italy from Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, and Albania.

text: What is the capital city of Finland, situated on the shore of the Gulf of Finland?
explanation: Helsinki was made capital of Finland in 1812 under Russian rule, replacing the historic capital of Turku.

text: Which river forms a substantial portion of the border between the United States and Mexico?
explanation: Known as the Rio Bravo in Mexico, the Rio Grande forms a large section of the US-Mexico border.

text: What is the capital city of Senegal, located on the westernmost point of mainland Africa?
explanation: Dakar sits on the Cap-Vert peninsula, marking the westernmost extremity of the African continent.

text: Which famous volcano in southern Italy destroyed the city of Pompeii in 79 AD?
explanation: Mount Vesuvius overlooks the Bay of Naples and is the only active volcano on the European mainland.

text: What is the largest lake in Africa by surface area?
explanation: Covering roughly 68,800 square kilometres, Lake Victoria is shared by Tanzania, Uganda, and Kenya.

text: Which river is the longest flowing entirely within France and emptying into the Atlantic Ocean?
explanation: The Loire runs for 1,006 kilometres and its valley is famous for its numerous historic châteaux.

text: What is the capital city of the Republic of Ireland?
explanation: Dublin is situated at the mouth of the River Liffey on the eastern coast of Ireland.

text: Which vast semi-arid desert covers large portions of Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa?
explanation: The Kalahari Desert spans roughly 900,000 square kilometres across southern Africa.

text: Which mountain range extends across Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia?
explanation: The Atlas Mountains stretch approximately 2,500 kilometres across the Maghreb in north-western Africa.

text: What is the capital city of South Korea?
explanation: Seoul lies on the Han River and forms the cultural, financial, and political heart of South Korea.

text: What is the highest mountain peak in Algeria, located in the Hoggar Mountains?
explanation: Mount Tahat rises to 2,908 metres in the Hoggar range, whereas Mount Chélia is the highest peak in the Aurès Mountains.

text: Which is the second-highest peak in Morocco and North Africa, after Mount Toubkal?
explanation: Mount Ouanoukrim rises to 4,089 metres, narrowly surpassing Mount M'Goun which stands at 4,071 metres.

text: Which river forms part of the natural border between Mali and Senegal before joining the Senegal River?
explanation: The Falémé River is a major tributary of the Senegal River and demarcates a substantial stretch of the Mali-Senegal border.

text: What is the lowest natural point on the African continent, situated at approximately 155 metres below sea level?
explanation: Lake Assal in Djibouti lies at 155 metres below sea level and is one of the most saline bodies of water on Earth.

text: What is the highest mountain peak on the Arabian Peninsula, rising above 3,660 metres?
explanation: Jabal an-Nabi Shu'ayb is located in Yemen near Sana'a and represents the highest elevation in the Arabian Peninsula.

text: In which country is the Deriba Caldera, which became its highest point following the 2011 partition?
explanation: The Deriba Caldera in the Marrah Mountains rises to 3,042 metres and is the highest peak in Sudan.

text: Which is the largest island in the Persian Gulf by surface area?
explanation: The Iranian island of Qeshm spans approximately 1,491 square kilometres, making it by far the largest in the Gulf.

text: Which strait connects the Gulf of Aqaba to the Red Sea, separating the Sinai Peninsula from Saudi Arabia?
explanation: The Strait of Tiran commands the sea passage from the Red Sea into the Gulf of Aqaba.

text: What is the highest mountain peak in Lebanon, rising to 3,088 metres in the Mount Lebanon range?
explanation: Qurnat as Sawda' reaches an elevation of 3,088 metres, making it the highest point in both Lebanon and the Levant.

text: Which is the longest river flowing entirely within the geographic borders of Morocco?
explanation: The Oum Er-Rbia flows for about 555 kilometres from the Middle Atlas to the Atlantic Ocean at Azemmour.

text: Which is the second-largest island in the Socotra Archipelago after Socotra Island itself?
explanation: Abd al Kuri covers roughly 133 square kilometres and lies between Socotra and the Somali coast.

text: What is the highest mountain peak in Iraq, situated in the Zagros Mountains near the Iranian border?
explanation: Cheekha Dar stands at 3,611 metres and is officially recognised as the highest summit in Iraq.

text: Which Moroccan mountain pass in the High Atlas, standing at 2,260 metres, connects Marrakech with Ouarzazate?
explanation: Tizi n'Tichka reaches an elevation of 2,260 metres and forms the premier vehicular crossing over the High Atlas.

text: What is the deepest known location in the Mediterranean Sea, situated in the Ionian Sea off Greece?
explanation: Calypso Deep plunges to approximately 5,267 metres below surface level in the Hellenic Trench.

text: Which is the longest river situated entirely within Lebanon, emptying into the Mediterranean north of Tyre?
explanation: The Litani River flows for roughly 140 kilometres entirely inside Lebanon, draining the southern Bekaa Valley.

text: What is the highest mountain peak of the Anti-Atlas range in Morocco?
explanation: Jbel Sirwa is an extinct stratovolcano rising to 3,304 metres, making it the apex of the Anti-Atlas.

text: In which country is the Ennedi Plateau, famous for its sandstone arches and designated a UNESCO World Heritage site?
explanation: The Ennedi Plateau lies in north-eastern Chad and features dramatic natural sandstone arches and ancient rock art.

text: What is the official political and constitutional capital of Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire) since 1983?
explanation: Yamoussoukro was designated the political capital in 1983, while Abidjan remains the economic metropolis.

text: What is the lowest natural point in Algeria, lying roughly 40 metres below sea level?
explanation: Chott Melrhir is an endorheic salt lake in south-eastern Algeria that drops to about 40 metres below sea level.

text: Which river forms the southern border of Namibia with South Africa before discharging into the Atlantic Ocean?
explanation: The Orange River originates in the Drakensberg mountains and defines the border between South Africa and Namibia.

text: What is the highest mountain peak in the Hajar Mountains of Oman, reaching approximately 3,009 metres?
explanation: Jebel Shams is the tallest peak in Oman and overlooks the deep canyon of Wadi an Nakhur.

text: In which country is the Cap-Vert peninsula, which forms the westernmost point of the mainland African continent?
explanation: The Cap-Vert peninsula is situated in Senegal and provides the location for its capital city, Dakar.

text: Which vast desert depression in north-western Egypt plunges to 133 metres below sea level?
explanation: The Qattara Depression spans roughly 19,605 square kilometres and is Africa's second-lowest land point.

text: Which peak is the highest mountain in Egypt, situated in the South Sinai Governorate at 2,629 metres?
explanation: Mount Catherine (Gabal Katrîna) is Egypt's highest summit, surpassing the nearby Mount Sinai.

text: What is the largest island in the Tunisian archipelago of Kerkennah, situated off the coast of Sfax?
explanation: Chergui, also referred to as Grande Kerkennah, constitutes the largest landmass of the Kerkennah Islands.

text: What is the highest mountain peak in the Drakensberg range and the highest point in Southern Africa?
explanation: Thabana Ntlenyana rises to 3,482 metres in Lesotho, making it the highest elevation in Southern Africa.

text: Djibouti shares Lake Abbe, renowned for its dramatic natural limestone chimneys, with which neighbouring country?
explanation: Lake Abbe sits directly on the border between Djibouti and Ethiopia within the Afar Depression.

text: Which major African river is the only river in the world that crosses the Equator twice?
explanation: The Congo River traces a colossal arc across Central Africa, cutting across the Equator once northward and once southward.

text: What is the highest mountain peak in Tunisia, located in the Kasserine Governorate?
explanation: Jebel ech Chambi reaches an elevation of 1,544 metres and is the highest geographical point in Tunisia.

text: Which body of water is connected to the Red Sea via the Bab-el-Mandeb strait?
explanation: Bab-el-Mandeb acts as the strategic choke point connecting the southern Red Sea directly to the Gulf of Aden.

text: Uganda shares the glaciated Rwenzori Mountains, often called the 'Mountains of the Moon', with which country?
explanation: The Rwenzori chain straddles the frontier between Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

text: What town serves as the regional capital of the historic Adrar Region in north-central Mauritania?
explanation: Atar is the administrative capital of Mauritania's Adrar Region, while Chinguetti is an ancient caravan centre nearby.

text: Which stratovolcano is the highest mountain in Iran and the tallest volcano in the entire Middle East?
explanation: Mount Damavand stands at 5,610 metres in the Alborz mountain range of northern Iran.

text: What is the highest mountain summit in Syria, situated along its south-western border with Lebanon?
explanation: Mount Hermon (Jabal al-Shaykh) peaks at 2,814 metres, forming the highest topographic point in Syria.

text: Which large endorheic salt lake in south-western Tunisia is the largest salt pan in the Sahara Desert?
explanation: Chott el Djerid encompasses roughly 5,000 square kilometres of salt flats between Tozeur and Kebili.

text: Zambia shares Lake Kariba, one of the world's largest man-made reservoirs by volume, with which country?
explanation: Lake Kariba was flooded by damming the Zambezi River along the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.

text: What is the name of the maritime passage separating the Socotra Archipelago from the Horn of Africa?
explanation: The Guardafui Channel runs between Cape Guardafui on the Somali mainland and the island of Socotra.

text: Which desert lies encircled inside the great bend of the Nile River in northern Sudan?
explanation: The Bayuda Desert occupies the loop of the Nile and is noted for its volcanic craters and black basalt plains.

text: The Caprivi Strip is a distinctive narrow salient of territory belonging to which Southern African nation?
explanation: The Caprivi Strip extends eastward from north-eastern Namibia, granting it strategic access to the Zambezi River.

text: Which country won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
explanation: Uruguay won the inaugural FIFA World Cup in 1930, defeating Argentina in the final.

text: How many players from one team are on the pitch at the start of a football match?
explanation: A football team fields 11 players on the pitch, including the goalkeeper.

text: Which nation has won the FIFA World Cup the most times?
explanation: Brazil holds the record with five World Cup victories, won in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, and 2002.

text: In which sport is the prestigious Wimbledon tournament played?
explanation: Wimbledon is the world's oldest and most prestigious tennis tournament, played on grass in London.

text: Which sprint event is considered the blue-riband event of athletics?
explanation: The 100 metres is the blue-riband sprint event, traditionally crowning the world's fastest humans.

text: What colour card does a football referee show to send off a player immediately?
explanation: A red card is shown by the referee to dismiss a player from the field of play.

text: In which country did the ancient Olympic Games originate?
explanation: The ancient Olympic Games originated in Olympia, ancient Greece, dating back to 776 BC.

text: What is the famous nickname of the Egypt national football team?
explanation: The Egyptian national football team is widely known as The Pharaohs, celebrating the country's ancient heritage.

text: Which nation won the 1998 FIFA World Cup on home soil?
explanation: France won their first World Cup title in 1998 by defeating Brazil 3-0 in the final.

text: What is the standard duration of a football match without extra time?
explanation: A regular football match lasts 90 minutes, played in two halves of 45 minutes each.

text: What piece of equipment do players use to hit the ball in tennis?
explanation: Tennis players use a strung racket to hit the tennis ball across the net.

text: Which Moroccan athlete won Olympic gold in both the 1500m and 5000m at Athens 2004?
explanation: Hicham El Guerrouj achieved a historic double by winning gold in both the 1500m and 5000m at the 2004 Athens Games.

text: Which country hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup, the first ever held in Africa?
explanation: South Africa hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup, making it the first African country to host the tournament.

text: How many years are there normally between Summer Olympic Games?
explanation: The Summer Olympic Games are traditionally celebrated every four years in an Olympiad.

text: Which legendary Jamaican sprinter won eight Olympic gold medals?
explanation: Usain Bolt dominated sprinting by winning eight Olympic gold medals across the 2008, 2012, and 2016 Games.

text: Which national team won the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar?
explanation: Argentina won the 2022 World Cup after defeating France in a penalty shootout in the final.

text: On which playing surface is the Roland Garros tennis tournament played?
explanation: The French Open at Roland Garros is famously played on red clay courts.

text: What object is passed between runners in an athletics relay race?
explanation: Relay team runners pass a baton to each other within a designated exchange zone.

text: Which Brazilian football legend won three FIFA World Cups in 1958, 1962, and 1970?
explanation: Pelé is the only football player in history to have won three FIFA World Cup trophies.

text: Which Greek city hosted the 2004 Summer Olympic Games?
explanation: The Olympic Games returned to their historic birthplace of Athens in the summer of 2004.

text: In tennis scoring, what does the term 'love' represent?
explanation: In tennis terminology, 'love' means a score of zero for that game or set.

text: Which country won the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) in 2019 in Egypt?
explanation: Algeria won the 2019 Africa Cup of Nations by beating Senegal 1-0 in the final in Cairo.

text: What is the official shape of a standard football according to the rules?
explanation: The official IFAB Laws of the Game require the football to be spherical.

text: Which British city hosted the 2012 Summer Olympic Games?
explanation: London hosted the Summer Olympics in 2012, becoming the first city to host the modern Games three times.

text: What was the name of the original trophy awarded to FIFA World Cup winners before 1974?
explanation: The Jules Rimet Trophy was awarded to World Cup champions until Brazil earned permanent ownership of it in 1970.

text: In tennis, what term describes a tied score of 40-40 in a single game?
explanation: A 40-40 score is called deuce, requiring a player to win two consecutive points to take the game.

text: Which part of the body cannot be intentionally used by outfield football players to touch the ball?
explanation: Outfield players are prohibited from deliberately touching the ball with their hands or arms during play.

text: Which country hosted the 1970 FIFA World Cup won by Brazil?
explanation: Mexico hosted the 1970 World Cup, famous for Brazil's legendary attacking team and Pelé's third title.

text: What colour medal is traditionally awarded to the winner of an Olympic event?
explanation: The winner of an Olympic event receives a gold medal, with silver for second and bronze for third.

text: How many Grand Slam tournaments are played in professional tennis each year?
explanation: The tennis Grand Slam consists of four majors: the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open.

text: In the Olympic motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius', what does the Latin word 'Citius' mean?
explanation: The historic Olympic motto translates into English as 'Faster, Higher, Stronger'.

text: In which year did Morocco win its sole Africa Cup of Nations football title in Ethiopia?
explanation: Morocco claimed its only AFCON title in 1976 during the tournament hosted by Ethiopia.

text: What is the standard running distance of the innermost lane of an athletics track?
explanation: A standard Olympic running track measures exactly 400 metres around the innermost lane.

text: How many substitutions per team are permanently permitted during regulation time in modern football?
explanation: IFAB rules permanently allow teams up to five substitutions during regular 90-minute matches.

text: In tennis, what term describes a legal serve that lands untouched by the receiver?
explanation: An ace occurs when a legal serve lands in the service box and the opponent fails to touch it.

text: Which was the first African nation to reach the quarter-finals of the FIFA World Cup?
explanation: Cameroon reached the quarter-finals at Italia 1990, led by veteran forward Roger Milla.

text: Which national team won the inaugural Africa Cup of Nations in 1957?
explanation: Egypt won the first tournament held in Khartoum in 1957, which featured only three participating teams.

text: Who was the first Arab woman to win an Olympic gold medal?
explanation: Moroccan athlete Nawal El Moutawakel won gold in the 400m hurdles at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.

text: Which tennis player achieved the 'Golden Slam' in 1988 by winning all four majors and Olympic singles gold?
explanation: Steffi Graf won all four Grand Slam singles titles and the Olympic gold medal in Seoul in 1988.

text: Which Moroccan runner achieved a historic 1,500m and 5,000m double gold at the 2004 Athens Olympics?
explanation: Hicham El Guerrouj won both the 1,500m and 5,000m titles in Athens, matching Paavo Nurmi's 1924 feat.

text: Which was the first African nation to qualify for a FIFA World Cup, doing so in 1934?
explanation: Egypt qualified for the 1934 tournament in Italy, becoming the first African and Arab team to participate.

text: Who was the first African footballer to win the Ballon d'Or?
explanation: Liberia's George Weah won the prestigious award in 1995 while playing for Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan.

text: Which of the four Grand Slam tennis tournaments is played exclusively on clay courts?
explanation: Roland Garros, held in Paris, is the only Grand Slam tournament contested on clay.

text: Which African nation won the gold medal in men's football at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics?
explanation: Nigeria became the first African nation to win Olympic football gold by defeating Argentina 3-2 in the final.

text: Which country won back-to-back FIFA World Cup titles in 1934 and 1938?
explanation: Italy became the first nation to retain the World Cup, managed on both occasions by Vittorio Pozzo.

text: Which Algerian athlete won the women's 1,500m gold medal at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics?
explanation: Hassiba Boulmerka won Algeria's first-ever Olympic gold medal with her victory in Barcelona.

text: Who won five consecutive Wimbledon men's singles titles between 2003 and 2007?
explanation: Roger Federer matched Björn Borg's Open Era record by winning five successive Wimbledon crowns.

text: Who was the first player to score a hat-trick in a FIFA World Cup final?
explanation: England's Geoff Hurst scored three times against West Germany in the 1966 final at Wembley.

text: Which nation caused a massive upset by winning the UEFA European Championship in 2004?
explanation: Greece defeated host nation Portugal 1-0 in the final in Lisbon to claim an improbable European title.

text: Which Greek athlete won the first modern Olympic marathon in Athens in 1896?
explanation: Spyridon Louis became a national hero in Greece by winning the inaugural modern Olympic marathon.

text: Which country won the Africa Cup of Nations in 2004 as host nation?
explanation: Tunisia claimed their first continental title in 2004 by defeating Morocco 2-1 in the final.

text: How many Grand Slam singles titles did Serena Williams win in the Open Era?
explanation: Serena Williams won 23 Grand Slam singles crowns, the most by any player in the Open Era.

text: Which footballer scored the famous 'Hand of God' goal against England at the 1986 World Cup?
explanation: Diego Maradona scored the controversial goal with his hand before adding the acclaimed 'Goal of the Century'.

text: In which city did Ethiopia's Abebe Bikila win the 1960 Olympic marathon running barefoot?
explanation: Bikila completed the marathon barefoot through Rome in 1960, becoming Sub-Saharan Africa's first Olympic gold medallist.

text: Who is the only goalkeeper to have won the prestigious Ballon d'Or award (in 1963)?
explanation: Soviet goalkeeper Lev Yashin, known as the 'Black Spider', remains the only goalkeeper to win the award.

text: Which Ethiopian distance runner won the 10,000m gold at both the 1996 and 2000 Olympic Games?
explanation: Haile Gebrselassie captured back-to-back 10,000-metre Olympic titles in Atlanta and Sydney.

text: Which national team won the 1976 Africa Cup of Nations held in Ethiopia?
explanation: Morocco clinched their sole AFCON title in 1976 by finishing top of the final round-robin group.

text: Which Spanish city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 1992?
explanation: Barcelona hosted the 1992 Olympics, famous for the appearance of the USA basketball 'Dream Team'.

text: Which Czech runner won gold in the 5,000m, 10,000m, and marathon at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics?
explanation: Emil Zátopek, nicknamed the 'Czech Locomotive', completed an unprecedented distance-running triple in 1952.

text: Which country won the gold medal in men's football at the 2000 Sydney Olympics?
explanation: Cameroon defeated Spain in a penalty shootout in Sydney to claim their first Olympic football gold medal.

text: Which Croatian tennis player won the 2001 Wimbledon men's singles title as a wildcard entrant?
explanation: Goran Ivanišević won Wimbledon in 2001, becoming the lowest-ranked and only wildcard player to do so.

text: Who was the first athlete in history to run a sub-four-minute mile, achieving the feat in 1954?
explanation: British athlete Roger Bannister ran the historic mile in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds on 6 May 1954.

text: Which player scored the very first goal in FIFA World Cup history in 1930?
explanation: French player Lucien Laurent scored the first-ever World Cup goal on 13 July 1930 against Mexico.

text: Who scored the fastest goal in FIFA World Cup history, timed at just 11 seconds from kick-off?
explanation: Turkey's Hakan Şükür scored after just 10.8 seconds against South Korea in the third-place play-off in 2002.

text: Who was the first tennis player in history to achieve a calendar-year 'Golden Slam'?
explanation: Steffi Graf achieved this feat in 1988 by winning all four Grand Slam singles titles and the Olympic gold medal in Seoul.

text: In which city were the modern Olympic Games held for the first time outside Europe?
explanation: The 1904 Summer Olympics were held in St. Louis, Missouri, making it the first Games hosted outside Europe.

text: Who is the only player to have scored in every single match his team played during a victorious World Cup campaign?
explanation: Brazil's Jairzinho scored in all six matches of Brazil's triumphant campaign at the 1970 World Cup in Mexico.

text: Who is the only male tennis player to win all four Grand Slam singles titles in a calendar year twice?
explanation: Australian Rod Laver achieved the calendar Grand Slam twice, first in 1962 and again in 1969.

text: Who scored the winning golden goal for France in extra time of the UEFA Euro 2000 final against Italy?
explanation: David Trezeguet scored a half-volley in the 103rd minute to win the tournament for France.

text: Which country won the gold medal in the first official Olympic football tournament for national teams in 1908?
explanation: Great Britain won the gold medal at the 1908 London Games by beating Denmark 2-0 in the final.

text: Which legendary track and field athlete won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics?
explanation: American athlete Jesse Owens famously won gold in the 100m, 200m, 4x100m relay, and long jump in Berlin.

text: Who was the first male tennis player to reach the milestone of 20 Grand Slam singles titles?
explanation: Switzerland's Roger Federer became the first man to win 20 Grand Slam singles titles at the 2018 Australian Open.

text: What was the nationality of referee Ali Bin Nasser, who officiated the famous 1986 Argentina vs England match?
explanation: Tunisian referee Ali Bin Nasser was the match official for the 1986 quarter-final featuring Maradona's famous goals.

text: Which powerhouse national team was upset by West Germany in the 1954 World Cup final known as the 'Miracle of Bern'?
explanation: The famed 'Mighty Magyars' of Hungary were surprisingly defeated 3-2 after leading 2-0 early in the match.

text: Who was the first Egyptian and Arab athlete to win an Olympic gold medal, achieving the feat in 1928?
explanation: Weightlifter El Sayed Nosseir won the light-heavyweight gold medal at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympic Games.

text: In which FIFA World Cup tournament were yellow and red cards introduced for the very first time?
explanation: Cards were first used at the 1970 World Cup in Mexico, having been devised by English referee Ken Aston.

text: Who was the first unseeded player in the Open Era to win the Wimbledon Gentlemen's Singles title?
explanation: Boris Becker won Wimbledon in 1985 as an unseeded player, becoming the champion at just 17 years old.

text: Which country hosted the 1992 Africa Cup of Nations, the first edition to feature 12 teams?
explanation: Senegal hosted the 1992 tournament, which was won by Ivory Coast in a historic penalty shootout against Ghana.

text: At which Olympic Games did Dick Fosbury revolutionize the high jump with his backward 'flop' technique?
explanation: Dick Fosbury won the gold medal at Mexico City 1968 using his revolutionary back-first high jump technique.

text: Which national team won the inaugural FIFA Women's World Cup held in China in 1991?
explanation: The United States won the inaugural Women's World Cup in 1991, defeating Norway 2-1 in the final.

text: Who was the manager of Morocco when they topped their group to reach the round of 16 at the 1986 World Cup?
explanation: Brazilian manager José 'Mehdi' Faria coached Morocco as they became the first African team to reach the knockout stage.

text: Which legendary stadium hosted the final match of two separate FIFA World Cups, in 1970 and 1986?
explanation: Mexico City's Estadio Azteca hosted the 1970 final won by Brazil and the 1986 final won by Argentina.

text: How old was Boris Becker when he became the youngest-ever Wimbledon Men's Singles champion in 1985?
explanation: Becker won the prestigious title at the age of just 17 years and 228 days, a record that remains intact.

text: Which athlete completed the 5,000m and 10,000m 'double-double' by winning both events at London 2012 and Rio 2016?
explanation: Great Britain's Mo Farah won four Olympic gold medals by defending his 5,000m and 10,000m titles in 2012 and 2016.

text: In which year did Morocco make its official debut appearance at the Summer Olympic Games?
explanation: Morocco debuted at the 1960 Rome Olympics, where Rhadi Ben Abdesselam claimed silver in the men's marathon.

text: Which country won the inaugural European Football Championship (Euro) in 1960?
explanation: The Soviet Union won the 1960 tournament in Paris, defeating Yugoslavia 2-1 after extra time in the final.

text: At the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, Emil Zátopek won gold in the 5,000m, 10,000m, and which other event?
explanation: Zátopek completed an unmatched Olympic distance treble by winning the marathon in his very first attempt at the distance.

text: Which is the first surah in the order of the Holy Quran?
explanation: Surah Al-Fatiha (The Opening) is the first chapter of the Quran and is recited in every unit of prayer.

text: How many pillars of Islam are there?
explanation: There are five pillars in Islam: Shahada (faith), Salah (prayer), Zakat (alms), Sawm (fasting), and Hajj (pilgrimage).

text: Which prophet is given the title "Khalilullah" (the intimate friend of God)?
explanation: Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) is revered as Khalilullah and is celebrated as the patriarch of monotheism.

text: Towards which sacred site do Muslims across the world turn during prayer?
explanation: The Kaaba, located in the Grand Mosque of Mecca, is the Qibla (focal point) for Islamic daily prayers.

text: Which prophet was commanded by God to build the Ark to survive the Great Flood?
explanation: Prophet Nuh (Noah) built the Ark under divine guidance to preserve the believers and pairs of all living creatures.

text: To which city did the Prophet Muhammad migrate from Mecca during the Hijra?
explanation: The Prophet migrated to Yathrib, subsequently renamed Medina, marking the start of the Islamic calendar.

text: Who was the first wife of the Prophet Muhammad?
explanation: Khadija bint Khuwaylid was the first wife of the Prophet and the very first person to accept Islam.

text: Which is the longest chapter (surah) in the Holy Quran?
explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow) is the longest surah in the Quran, consisting of 286 verses.

text: Which angel was tasked with bringing divine revelation to the prophets?
explanation: The Archangel Jibril (Gabriel) carried God's revelation to the prophets, including Prophet Muhammad.

text: Which holy book was revealed to Prophet Dawud (David)?
explanation: The Zabur (Psalms) is the scripture given to Prophet Dawud (David) according to the Quran.

text: In which cave was Prophet Muhammad meditating when he received his first revelation?
explanation: The first revelation descended upon Prophet Muhammad in the Cave of Hira on the Mountain of Light (Jabal al-Nour).

text: Who was the first Rashidun caliph following the death of Prophet Muhammad?
explanation: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was chosen as the first successor (caliph) to lead the Muslim community.

text: In which Moroccan city did Fatima al-Fihri establish the historic Al-Qarawiyyin university?
explanation: Fatima al-Fihri founded Al-Qarawiyyin in Fes in 859 CE, recognized as the world's oldest continually operating university.

text: Which famous Islamic palace and fortress complex is located in Granada, Andalusia?
explanation: The Alhambra in Granada is one of the most celebrated masterworks of Islamic architecture in Islamic Spain.

text: Which blessed night in Ramadan is described in the Quran as better than a thousand months?
explanation: Laylat al-Qadr (The Night of Power or Decree) marks the commencement of the Quranic revelation.

text: Which prophet was swallowed by a large fish and then delivered safely by God?
explanation: Prophet Yunus (Jonah) called upon God from within the belly of the great fish and was delivered.

text: Which mosque located in Jerusalem is the third holiest site in Islam?
explanation: Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem was Islam's first Qibla and is the third holiest site after Mecca and Medina.

text: What is the name of the ritual call to prayer in Islam?
explanation: The Adhan is the Islamic call to prayer recited by the muezzin to summon believers to congregational worship.

text: Who is the mother of Prophet Isa (Jesus) according to the Holy Quran?
explanation: Maryam (Mary) is the mother of Prophet Isa and the only woman explicitly named in the Quran, having a surah named after her.

text: Which famed Muslim explorer and traveller was born in Tangier, Morocco, and known for his vast journeys?
explanation: Ibn Battuta travelled over 70,000 miles throughout Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, and China during the 14th century.

text: Which pillar of Islam refers to the obligatory almsgiving to the poor and needy?
explanation: Zakat is the compulsory social purification tax giving a set percentage of savings to the impoverished.

text: Which prophet spoke directly with God and earned the title "Kalimullah"?
explanation: Prophet Musa (Moses) is known as Kalimullah because God spoke to him directly on Mount Sinai.

text: Which is the shortest chapter (surah) in the Holy Quran in number of verses?
explanation: Surah Al-Kawthar is the shortest surah in the Holy Quran, consisting of merely three verses.

text: What was the name of the Prophet Muhammad's father?
explanation: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib passed away shortly before his son Prophet Muhammad was born.

text: What is the name of the mountain where God spoke to Prophet Moses in the Sinai peninsula?
explanation: Mount Sinai, referred to as Jabal Al-Tur in Arabic, is the mountain where Moses received the divine commandments.

text: Which Muslim golden age scholar is recognized as the father of algebra?
explanation: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi wrote the foundational book from which the word 'algebra' originates.

text: Which Islamic holiday coincides with the Hajj pilgrimage and involves the ritual sacrifice of livestock?
explanation: Eid al-Adha (Festival of the Sacrifice) falls on the 10th day of Dhu al-Hijjah during the Hajj season.

text: In which Moroccan city is the renowned Hassan II Mosque located overlooking the ocean?
explanation: The Hassan II Mosque is situated in Casablanca, featuring an iconic tall minaret right by the Atlantic Ocean.

text: Which historical event marks the starting point of the Islamic Hijri calendar?
explanation: The Hijra, the migration of Prophet Muhammad and his followers from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE, inaugurated the Hijri era.

text: What is the name of the sacred well located near the Kaaba within the Grand Mosque of Mecca?
explanation: The Zamzam well sprang forth miraculously to provide water for Hajar and her infant son Isma'il.

text: Which prophet is renowned in Islamic tradition for his extraordinary patience through illness and suffering?
explanation: Prophet Ayyub (Job) is celebrated as the paragon of steadfast patience in the face of immense adversity.

text: What is the architectural tower of a mosque called from which the call to prayer is traditionally announced?
explanation: A minaret is the distinctive tower of a mosque historically climbed by the muezzin to deliver the call to prayer.

text: Which is the only chapter (surah) in the Holy Quran that does not begin with the Basmala?
explanation: Surah At-Tawbah (The Repentance) is the sole chapter in the Quran that does not open with the Basmala.

text: Which celebrated Muslim physician and philosopher authored the influential medical encyclopedia "The Canon of Medicine"?
explanation: Avicenna (Ibn Sina) composed 'The Canon of Medicine', which remained a standard medical authority in Europe and the Islamic world for centuries.

text: Which companion and third Rashidun caliph was honored with the title "Dhun-Nurayn" (Possessor of the Two Lights)?
explanation: Uthman ibn Affan received this title because he married two daughters of Prophet Muhammad: Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum.

text: Which companion was chosen by Prophet Muhammad to be the very first muezzin in Islam?
explanation: Bilal ibn Rabah was chosen for his resonant, melodious voice and became the first caller to prayer in Islamic history.

text: On which mount do Muslim pilgrims gather on the ninth day of Dhu al-Hijjah during Hajj?
explanation: Gathering at the plain and Mount of Arafat is the central rite and culmination of the annual Hajj pilgrimage.

text: Which renowned North African historian and scholar authored "The Muqaddimah" and is considered a founder of sociology?
explanation: Ibn Khaldun established fundamental concepts in historiography and sociology in his masterwork 'The Muqaddimah'.

text: On which day of the week do Muslims gather for the special congregational midday prayer and sermon?
explanation: Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah) is considered the weekly day of assembly where Muslims attend the khutbah (sermon) and congregational prayer.

text: Which woman founded the University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco?
explanation: Fatima al-Fihri founded the al-Qarawiyyin mosque and university in 859 CE, considered the oldest continuously operating university.

text: During the reign of which Rightly Guided Caliph was the official standardized codex of the Quran compiled?
explanation: Uthman ibn Affan commissioned the standardisation of the Quranic text and distributed copies across the empire.

text: Which Umayyad caliph ordered the construction of the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem?
explanation: Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan commissioned the Dome of the Rock, which was completed around 691 CE.

text: What was the historical name of Medina before the Prophet's migration (Hijrah)?
explanation: Medina was originally known as Yathrib before the Prophet's arrival transformed it into Madinat al-Nabi.

text: Which ruler, nicknamed the 'Falcon of Quraysh', founded the Umayyad dynasty in al-Andalus?
explanation: Abd al-Rahman I survived the Abbasid purge and established the independent Umayyad emirate of Cordoba in 756 CE.

text: Which scholar of Andalusian descent authored the celebrated historical work 'The Muqaddimah'?
explanation: Ibn Khaldun pioneered early sociology, economics, and historiography in his masterpiece, The Muqaddimah.

text: In which Gregorian calendar year did the Hijrah take place, marking the start of the Islamic era?
explanation: The Prophet's migration from Mecca to Medina took place in 622 CE, which caliph Umar later set as year 1 AH.

text: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish before being delivered by God?
explanation: Prophet Yunus, also referred to as Dhul-Nun, was preserved inside a whale or large fish after supplicating God.

text: What was the name of the grand library and translation institute in Abbasid Baghdad?
explanation: The House of Wisdom was a major intellectual academy and translation hub during the Islamic Golden Age under Abbasid rule.

text: In which year of the Islamic calendar (AH) did the major Battle of Badr take place?
explanation: The Battle of Badr was fought on the 17th of Ramadan in the 2nd year after the Hijrah (624 CE).

text: Which famous explorer from Tangier travelled across the Islamic world and beyond for nearly thirty years?
explanation: Ibn Battuta left Tangier in 1325 CE, covering roughly 117,000 kilometres across Africa, the Middle East, and Asia.

text: Who is the only woman after whom an entire surah of the Quran is named?
explanation: Surah Maryam (Chapter 19) is the only surah in the Quran named explicitly after a woman.

text: Which master Ottoman imperial architect designed the Suleymaniye and Selimiye mosques?
explanation: Mimar Sinan served as chief royal architect of the Ottoman Empire, designing over 300 classic structures.

text: Which famous peace treaty was concluded between the Muslims and the Quraysh in 6 AH?
explanation: The Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah established a 10-year truce between Medina and Mecca, opening routes for diplomatic ties.

text: Which Andalusian philosopher and jurist from Cordoba is known in the Western world as Averroes?
explanation: Ibn Rushd, born in Cordoba, was renowned for his comprehensive commentaries on Aristotle and defence of philosophy.

text: Which chapter of the Quran is traditionally referred to as the 'Heart of the Quran'?
explanation: Surah Ya-Sin is widely known as the 'Heart of the Quran' due to its central focus on fundamental tenets like the resurrection.

text: Which astronomical instrument was greatly refined by Muslim scholars to determine prayer times and coordinates?
explanation: Medieval Muslim astronomers vastly advanced the astrolabe, adapting it for celestial mapping and religious timekeeping.

text: Which prophet is cited in the Quran as the foremost example of steadfast patience during severe illness and affliction?
explanation: Prophet Ayyub endured trials of severe sickness and loss with remarkable patience before God restored his health and family.

text: To which prophet were the Psalms (Zabur) revealed according to the Quran?
explanation: The Quran explicitly states that the Zabur (Psalms) was given by God to Prophet Dawud.

text: Which Moroccan dynasty, led by Yusuf ibn Tashfin, founded the city of Marrakech?
explanation: The Almoravids founded Marrakech around 1062 CE and established it as the imperial capital of their realm.

text: Which Muslim physician was the first to scientifically distinguish smallpox from measles?
explanation: Al-Razi wrote a landmark treatise outlining the distinct clinical features of smallpox and measles.

text: In which surah of the Quran does the phrase 'Bismillah' appear twice?
explanation: Surah An-Naml contains the Basmala at its beginning and again in verse 30 within Solomon's letter to Sheba.

text: Which Muslim scientist pioneered modern optics and authored the famous 'Book of Optics' (Kitab al-Manazir)?
explanation: Ibn al-Haytham established the foundations of modern optics, correctly explaining vision through light entering the eye.

text: Which Umayyad caliph commissioned the construction of the Great Umayyad Mosque in Damascus?
explanation: Caliph Al-Walid I commissioned the Great Umayyad Mosque in Damascus, completed in 715 CE.

text: Who was the very first person to accept Islam and believe in Prophet Muhammad's message?
explanation: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, the Prophet's wife, was the first person to believe in his divine revelation.

text: Which prophet was sent to the people of Thamud with a miraculous she-camel as a sign?
explanation: Prophet Salih was sent to guide the ancient tribe of Thamud, given a she-camel as a divine miracle.

text: Which dynasty founded the city of Cairo and established the historic Al-Azhar Mosque in 969 CE?
explanation: The Fatimid general Jawhar al-Siqilli founded Cairo and laid the foundation stones of Al-Azhar Mosque in 969 CE.

text: Which prophet spoke from the cradle as an infant according to the Quran?
explanation: The Quran recounts that Prophet Isa spoke as a newborn baby to defend his mother Maryam's honour.

text: Who were the two overseers appointed by Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan to direct the construction of the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem?
options: Ibn al-Muqaffa and Muhammad ibn al-Qasim
Khalid ibn Yazid and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib
Raja ibn Haywa and Yazid ibn Salam
Al-Hasan al-Basri and Ata ibn Abi Rabah
explanation: The scholar Raja ibn Haywa and the architect Yazid ibn Salam oversaw the monument's construction, completed in 72 AH (691–692 CE).

text: Who is the only Companion of the Prophet explicitly mentioned by name in the Holy Quran?
explanation: Zayd ibn Haritha is the sole companion named directly in the Quran, in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:37).

text: In which fortress in modern-day Algeria did Ibn Khaldun retreat to write his celebrated 'Muqaddimah'?
explanation: Ibn Khaldun stayed at the Fortress of Ibn Salama near Tiaret between 1375 and 1379, where he penned his monumental prolegomena.

text: Which is the only Surah in the Holy Quran that contains two prostrations of recitation (Sujud al-Tilawah)?
explanation: Surah Al-Hajj uniquely features two recitation prostrations, located at verse 18 and verse 77.

text: Which Andalusian polymath authored the foundational 30-volume medical and surgical compendium 'Kitab al-Tasrif'?
explanation: Known in Europe as Albucasis, Al-Zahrawi pioneered surgical instruments and illustrated over 200 tools in 'Kitab al-Tasrif'.

text: Which Muslim astronomer and engineer designed the famous Nilometer on Roda Island in Cairo in 861 CE?
explanation: Al-Farghani (known in Latin as Alfraganus) supervised the construction of the Roda Nilometer under the Abbasid Caliph al-Mutawakkil.

text: Which Nasrid ruler commissioned the construction of the famous 'Court of the Lions' in the Alhambra of Granada?
explanation: Sultan Muhammad V constructed the Court of the Lions and its surrounding halls during his second reign in the late 14th century.

text: Which Abbasid vizier and calligrapher established the codified system of proportioned script known as 'al-khatt al-mansub'?
explanation: Ibn Muqla developed the geometric system that proportioned Arabic letterforms based on the rhombic dot and the aleph.

text: Which Surah of the Quran was traditionally nicknamed 'Al-Fadiha' (The Exposer) for unveiling the secrets of hypocrites?
explanation: Surah At-Tawbah was called 'Al-Fadiha' because it thoroughly exposed the hidden deceits of the hypocrites around the expedition of Tabuk.

text: Which Muslim geographer created the famous world map 'Tabula Rogeriana' for King Roger II of Sicily in 1154?
explanation: Al-Idrisi compiled 'Nuzhat al-Mushtaq' and drew the most advanced world map of the medieval era while serving at the Norman court in Sicily.

text: Who was the Qurayshite envoy who negotiated and signed the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah with the Prophet in 6 AH?
explanation: Suhayl ibn Amr served as the lead Quraysh negotiator for the historic treaty, later embracing Islam at the conquest of Mecca.

text: Which astronomer directed the establishment of the renowned Maragha Observatory under the patronage of Hulagu Khan in 1259 CE?
explanation: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi founded the Maragha Observatory in northwestern Iran, producing the influential 'Zij-i Ilkhani' star tables.

text: Which Surah in the Holy Quran contains the Basmala formula twice?
explanation: Surah An-Naml opens with the Basmala and repeats it in verse 30 inside the letter from Prophet Solomon to the Queen of Sheba.

text: Which Umayyad Caliph founded the very first institutional Islamic hospital (bimaristan) in Damascus in 707 CE (88 AH)?
explanation: Caliph Al-Walid I established the first true bimaristan in Damascus, assigning salaried physicians and dedicated care for lepers.

text: What was the official name given to the city of Baghdad by its founder, the Abbasid Caliph Al-Mansur, upon its completion in 762 CE?
explanation: Caliph Al-Mansur officially designated his newly constructed round administrative capital as 'Madinat al-Salam' (City of Peace).

text: Which Andalusian polymath wrote 'The Incoherence of the Incoherence' (Tahafut al-Tahafut) defending philosophy against Al-Ghazali?
explanation: Ibn Rushd wrote 'Tahafut al-Tahafut' as a detailed refutation of Al-Ghazali's attack on Aristotelian metaphysics.

text: Which single word is the longest in the Holy Quran by letter count in Uthmanic orthography?
explanation: The word 'Fa-asqaynākumūhu' (فأسقيناكموه) in Surah Al-Hijr (15:22) comprises 11 letters, making it the longest single lexical unit.

text: Which companion was chosen by the Prophet as the first teacher and ambassador dispatched to Medina before the Hijrah?
explanation: Mus'ab ibn Umayr was sent to Yathrib after the First Pledge of al-Aqaba to instruct the early converts in Quran and prayer.

text: Which polymath authored the seminal 'Book of Optics' (Kitab al-Manazir), radically correcting classical theories of vision?
explanation: Known in the West as Alhazen, Ibn al-Haytham established through experimental proof that vision occurs via light entering the eye.

text: Under the reign of which Almohad caliph were the Hassan Tower in Rabat and the Giralda in Seville largely built?
explanation: Abu Yusuf Yaqub al-Mansur oversaw the height of Almohad architecture, including the construction of the Hassan Tower and Seville's minaret.

text: Which historic architectural landmark in Tunisia was founded in 670 CE (50 AH) by general Uqba ibn Nafi?
explanation: The Great Mosque of Kairouan, also known as the Mosque of Uqba, was built alongside the founding of the city of Kairouan.

text: Which Muslim polymath wrote the foundational encyclopaedic survey of Indian culture and science titled 'Tahqiq ma li-l-Hind'?
explanation: Al-Biruni mastered Sanskrit to write his exhaustive and impartial study of Indian society, astronomy, and religion around 1030 CE.

text: Which prominent Companion founded the garrison city of Kufa in Iraq under the instructions of Caliph Umar in 638 CE?
explanation: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas selected the site and designed the layout of Kufa following the victory at the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah.

text: Which lexicographer authored 'Lisan al-Arab', widely recognised as the most comprehensive dictionary of classical Arabic?
explanation: Ibn Manzur compiled 'Lisan al-Arab' in 1290 CE, integrating five major earlier lexicons into a massive 20-volume work.

text: Which Mamluk Sultan commanded the Muslim army to a decisive victory against the Mongols at the Battle of Ayn Jalut in 1260 CE?
explanation: Sultan Sayf al-Din Qutuz rallied his forces at Ayn Jalut, inflicting the first irreversible military defeat on the Mongol Empire.

text: Which prophet is mentioned by proper name the most times in the text of the Holy Quran?
explanation: The Prophet Musa (Moses) is mentioned by name 136 times across various Surahs of the Holy Quran.

text: What is the famous name of the spiralling helical minaret built for the Great Mosque of Samarra by Caliph al-Mutawakkil?
